title: Who Put Bella in the Wych Elm? Britain's Creepiest Unsolved Murder
description:
In April 1943, four boys hunting for bird's eggs in Hagley Wood, England stumbled onto a nightmare — a human skull hidden inside a hollow wych elm tree. Beneath it lay a nearly complete skeleton, taffeta fabric stuffed in the mouth, and one hand severed and buried thirteen feet away like a grim trophy.

Pathologist James Webster determined the woman had been dead since around October 1941. She was about 35 years old, just four foot ten, with crooked lower teeth and a gold ring found nearby. Despite the clues, dental records and missing persons reports turned up nothing. The case went cold — until eerie graffiti began appearing across Birmingham: 'Who put Bella down the Wych Elm?'

No one ever traced the writer. Was it a witness? The killer, taunting police? The graffiti kept reappearing on the same stone obelisk for over fifty years, last seen in 1999. To this day, Bella has never been identified, and her killer was never found.
